headline: Google Voice Search adds live chat, translation, and song recognition
summary: Google's Voice Search is getting a major overhaul, integrating live chat, real-time translation, and song identification into a single, more versatile tool.
details: Google Voice Search has been updated with a new interface and several powerful new features, making it a much more compelling option for users. Previously, the voice search would automatically start searching if you paused, but the new update includes a toggle for 'auto search,' allowing users to manually confirm when they are finished speaking.

The update introduces four new buttons that act as mode switchers. One button keeps the feature in standard search mode. Another opens a Gemini Live interface, enabling ongoing conversations within the Google app.

Song recognition, a feature previously present but less accessible, is now a dedicated mode, improving its usability in noisy environments. The 'Translate' mode allows the voice search to translate spoken words into another language, enhancing communication.

While some of these features existed within the broader Google app, their integration into Voice Search makes them immediately accessible to anyone using the feature. This transforms Voice Search from a simple search tool into a multi-functional assistant.

This significant enhancement positions Google Voice Search as a 'jack of all trades,' offering a wide range of functionalities from basic search to real-time translation and music identification, all within a single interface.
